name: Masacara
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Nikulin, Andrey. 2020. Proto-Macro-Jê: um estudo reconstrutivo. Doctoral thesis, Universidade de Brasília.
sources.note: §1.1.5: 'Para o Masakará[masa1311].. contamos com apenas uma lista coligida por Martius (1867, v. 2, p. 144-145)'; calls it the most divergent Kamakã language; Kamakã phonology explicitly not treated. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Ramirez, Henri, Valdir Vegini & Maria Cristina Victorino de França. 2015. Koropó, puri, kamakã e outras línguas do Leste Brasileiro. LIAMES 15(2): 223-277. doi:10.20396/liames.v15i2.8642302.
sources.note: Masakará treated pp. 249-252 (classification as the divergent branch of Kamakã, Maxakalí comparisons) and Anexo III pp. 269-274 (94-item Kamakã list with a Masakará column from Martius 1863: 144-145). p. 237 on the 19th-c. lists: 'O uso de acentos e outros diacríticos (V̀, V́, V̂, V̈, Vh) não vem acompanhado da devida explicação sobre os seus significados.' No stress statement.

sources.citation: Martins, Andérbio Márcio Silva. 2007. Revisão da família lingüística Kamakã proposta por Chestmir Loukotka. MA thesis, Universidade de Brasília. 89 pp.
sources.note: §3.5 'Fundamentação para manter na família lingüística Kamakã a língua Masakará' (pp. 48-50) and Anexo II reproduce Martius's Masakará forms (with his accents, e.g. pá, inkrú, guxá) for lexical/phonological correspondences; the words 'acento'/'tônica' do not occur in the thesis. Silent on stress.
sources.venue: MA thesis, Universidade de Brasília. 89 pp

sources.citation: Métraux, Alfred & Curt Nimuendajú. 1946. The Camacan linguistic family. In HSAI vol. 1, 547-552.
sources.note: Masacará mentioned only as one of the Camacan groups, 'near the São Francisco River, at Joazeiro'. Ethnographic; nothing on language sounds.

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1932. La familia lingüística Kamakan del Brasil. Revista del Instituto de Etnología de la Universidad Nacional de Tucumán 2: 493-524.
sources.note: Masakará data ('Ma.', from Martius pp. 144-145 and supplement pp. 545-546) enter the family comparison; p. 496-497 calls it 'un dialecto apenas diferenciado del Kamakan'. p. 498 'Fonética' only: 'Las vocales acentuadas están indicadas por un acento, las nasales por una tilde' — notational, no rule.
sources.venue: Revista del Instituto de Etnología de la Universidad Nacional de Tucumán

sources.citation: Martius, Carl Friedrich Philipp von. 1867. Beiträge zur Ethnographie und Sprachenkunde Amerika's zumal Brasiliens. II. Zur Sprachenkunde: Wörtersammlung Brasilianischer Sprachen / Glossaria linguarum Brasiliensium. Leipzig: Fleischer. 'Masacará', pp. 144-145.
sources.note: The sole primary record: c. 130 Latin-glossed items collected by Martius (M) and Spix (S) in 1819. Many forms carry an acute on a (usually final) vowel (gachtatózo, chighkó, kümghüáng, aggreamú, cottó, kumbüóh, pá, kügcrá, garé, gachthá, pacó, achar namú, khuúng, honí, ihntá, hingürá, kaichthüóh, anthó, mutgkú..), but the list has no key and the only footnote reads 'Vergl. I. 279. Der Name Masacará bedeutet in mehreren Tupi-Dialecten: die Hähne. — M = von Martius, S = von Spix aufgenommen.' The preface's accent convention (pp. 28-30, acute 'dient, den Vocal zu schärfen oder die Sylbe zu beton…

sources.citation: Spix, J. B. von & C. F. P. von Martius. 1828. Reise in Brasilien.. in den Jahren 1817 bis 1820, Bd. 2. München: Lindauer. pp. 702-703.
sources.note: Original travel-journal version of the same passage: 'Der Klang ihrer Worte war heisser, rauh und unangenehm; sie sprachen langsam und ohne lebhafte Betonung'. Nothing on word stress.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid masa1311 'Masacara'; Biblioteca Digital Curt Nimuendajú (etnolinguistica.org) pages familia:kamaka and lingua:masakara; Wikipedia (en) 'Masakará language'.
sources.note: Glottolog lists no descriptive reference (only Martius 1867 and Martins 2007 for existence/classification); the etnolinguistica.org Masakará ficha is empty; Wikipedia cites only Nikulin 2020, Loukotka 1968, Martins 2007 and says nothing on phonology. LIAMES site search for 'Masakará' returns no article beyond Ramirez et al. 2015 (found under 'Kamakã').

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1968. Classification of South American Indian languages. Los Angeles: UCLA Latin American Center.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Cited by Wikipedia and Ramirez et al. 2015 for Masakará; a classification with a few diagnostic forms, almost certainly no stress statement, listed only because it is the one remaining Masakará-citing work not opened.
